sections.title: THERE IS A SLGT RISK OF SVR TSTMS OVER THE NRN PLAINS
sections.text: ...SYNOPSIS... AN UPPER TROUGH WILL GRADUALLY SHIFT OFFSHORE THE E COAST THROUGH THE PERIOD...WITH HIGH PRESSURE BUILDING EWD ACROSS THE MS VALLEY AND INTO THE APPALACHIANS. TO THE W...AN UPPER RIDGE WILL EXIST ACROSS THE PLAINS...BUT WILL BREAK DOWN OVER THE NRN HIGH PLAINS LATE AS AN UPPER SHORTWAVE TROUGH MOVES ACROSS THE NRN ROCKIES. HERE...WEAK LOW PRESSURE WILL DEVELOP ALONG THE ERN MT BORDER BY AFTERNOON AHEAD OF A COLD FRONT WHICH WILL BE THE FOCUS FOR DEVELOPMENT DURING THE DAY...SPREADING EWD ACROSS THE DAKOTAS OVERNIGHT.

sections.title: NRN PLAINS
sections.text: THE WARM SECTOR WILL BE CAPPED THROUGH EARLY AFTERNOON E OF AN ADVANCING COLD FRONT OVER ERN MT...ALLOWING STRONG INSTABILITY TO DEVELOP FROM THERE INTO THE DAKOTAS. UPPER HEIGHT FALLS WITH THE TROUGH WILL OVERSPREAD THE AREA LATE...WITH INCREASING FORCING WITH TIME. STORMS ARE EXPECTED TO ORGANIZE OVER ERN MT/NERN WY BY LATE AFTERNOON...AND INCREASING IN INTENSITY AS THEY TREK INTO ND AND NRN SD. STEEP DEEP LAYER LAPSE RATES WILL FAVOR VIGOROUS UPDRAFTS...ALTHOUGH INITIALLY HIGH BASED. HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS WILL BE INCREASINGLY LIKELY AS THE ACTIVITY BECOMES BETTER ESTABLISHED...POSSIBLY ORGANIZING INTO A FORWARD PROPAGATING SYSTEM. RELATIVELY WEAK FLOW IN THE 850-700 MB LAYER AND SURGING OUTFLOW MAY MITIGATE AN OTHERWISE FAVORABLE PARAMETER SPACE FOR SIG HAIL...ALTHOUGH AN ISOLATED SIG HAIL REPORT CANNOT BE RULED OUT.

sections.title: ERN NEB/KS...NWRN MO AND SWRN IA
sections.text: INDICATIONS ARE THAT STORMS WILL BE ONGOING ACROSS THE MID MO VALLEY WITH A 30-40 KT SWLY LOW LEVEL JET EARLY. THIS ACTIVITY MAY BE CAPABLE OF MARGINALLY SEVERE HAIL. DURING THE DAY...A DIFFERENTIAL HEATING BOUNDARY WILL LIKELY EXIST OVER NERN KS...WITH THE POSSIBILITY OF FURTHER STRENGTHENING DURING THE AFTERNOON. LARGE HAIL AND GUSTY WINDS WILL BE POSSIBLE. ..JEWELL/LEITMAN.. 08/15/2011

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: WATER VAPOR IMAGERY DEPICTS A NUMBER OF SHORT WAVE TROUGHS/PV ANOMALIES SPREADING ACROSS THE PAC NW/NRN GREAT BASIN WITHIN BELT OF 40-50KT SWLY MID LEVEL FLOW. MODEL GUIDANCE INDICATES THAT PHASING WILL OCCUR BETWEEN SHORT WAVE CURRENTLY CROSSING OLYMPIC PENINSULA AND A TRAIN OF LOWER AMPLITUDE DISTURBANCES FROM NRN CA TO THE ROCKIES. HEIGHT FALLS OF 30-60M PER 12H AT 500MB ARE FORECAST TO SPREAD EAST FROM ID/MT LATER TODAY AND CONTRIBUTE TO LEE CYCLOGENESIS ACROSS ERN MT/WY. LEE LOW WILL THEN MOVE ACROSS THE DAKOTAS TONIGHT COINCIDENT WITH AMPLIFICATION OF UPPER SHORT WAVE TROUGH. AN UNSEASONABLY AMPLIFIED UPPER TROUGH SUFFUSED WITH HIGH PW VALUES WILL MAKE ONLY GRADUAL PROGRESS EAST ACROSS THE ATLANTIC SEABOARD TODAY. LIFT AND POCKETS OF GREATER DIURNAL DESTABILIZATION SHOULD LEAD TO MORE NUMEROUS TSTMS ACROSS THE NORTHEAST. A FEW STRONGER/PERSISTENT STORMS MAY DEVELOP WITHIN THE MDT/HVY RAIN SHIELD SPREADING ACROSS SRN/SERN NEW ENGLAND AS THE SURFACE LOW TRACKS NEWD ALONG COASTAL WARM FRONT LATER TODAY. ELSEWHERE...STORMS ARE EXPECTED TO DEVELOP ON AND AHEAD OF WEAK FRONT/WIND SHIFT TRAILING FROM THE EAST COAST SYSTEM INTO FL...AND ALSO OVER THE SOUTHWEST AND INTERMOUNTAIN REGIO

sections.title: MT/WY INTO DAKOTAS
sections.text: LOW LEVEL MOISTURE TRANSPORT BENEATH STEEP LAPSE RATE PLUME ON THE ERN FLANK OF LEE TROUGH/SURFACE LOW WILL CONTRIBUTE TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF STRONG POTENTIAL INSTABILITY FROM NERN MT ACROSS ND. SOME CLOUD COVER ACROSS THESE AREAS THIS MORNING...IN ADDITION TO STRONG CAPPING...WILL TEND TO INHIBIT DEEP CONVECTIVE INITIATION ACROSS THE MOST UNSTABLE AREAS UNTIL THE ARRIVAL OF STRONGER LARGE SCALE FORCING WITH THE UPPER TROUGH LATER THIS AFTERNOON THROUGH THIS EVENING. FARTHER WEST...TERRAIN INFLUENCES...WEAKER INHIBITION...AND STRONGER FORCING WITH THE UPPER TROUGH...WILL ALL CONTRIBUTE TO AN INCREASE IN HIGH-BASED TSTM DEVELOPMENT ACROSS THE ROCKIES FROM FAR ERN ID TO SWRN MT AND ACROSS WY. A FEW OF THESE STORMS COULD PRODUCE MARGINALLY SEVERE HAIL TO AN INCH IN DIAMETER AND GUSTY WINDS. HOWEVER...UNCERTAINTIES REGARDING GREATER DESTABILIZATION IN THESE AREAS PRECLUDES EXTENDING THE SLGT RISK WWD AT THIS TIME. AS SURFACE LOW/LEE TROUGH AND FRONT INTENSIFY AND ADVANCE EAST FROM MT/WY LATER TODAY...STORMS SHOULD LIKEWISE INTENSIFY AND ORGANIZE WITH GREATEST SEVERE WEATHER THREAT DEVELOPING EAST INTO ND. INITIALLY DISCRETE STORMS COULD BE SUPERCELLULAR GIVEN MORE THAN ADEQUATE DIRECTIO
